Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the reply of England Under-19. The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the players of Australia Under-19. It will be the skipper, Ben McKinney to open the innings for England Under-19 alongside Theo Wylie. Charlie Anderson has the new ball in hand and he is raring to go. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, England Under-19 need 267 runs to win and really challenge for that semi-final berth but Australia Under-19 are unbeaten and have some really good pacers. The onus is now on the English openers to give their team a head start in the game. Will they be able to do so though? We shall find out. Do join us soon as the run chase isn't far away.

The top performer with the ball for England Under-19, Theo Wylie is down for a chat. He says it was a good day out and there was turn in the deck that suited his bowling. He adds that he was trying to keep it on the stumps and the other spinner contributed nicely keeping it tight too. He then says they will have to play positively and put the bad balls away when it's there to be hit. He says there is depth and talent in the batting to get this chase done. He concludes with how he changed from pace bowling to spin and has never looked back since.

England Under-19 will be a tad disappointed in the end as they have ended up giving away at least 20 runs more than they would have liked. Sebastian Morgan bowled a brilliant spell up top and was well supported by the off-break bowler Farhan Ahmed from the other end. It was after the first Powerplay that they started to concede runs as the likes of Eddie Jack and Luc Benkenstein were hit away for boundaries. The spinners then pulled things back in the middle overs as Theo Wylie picked up wickets at regular intervals and even got one right at the death to make it a four-fer. Tazeem Ali too bowled well but Eddie Jack and then Noah Thain in that final over let things slip and now they have a big total to chase down.

Wow, that was some ending! A very well-fought first half of this brewing rivalry between the next generation of these two eternal rival nations but at the halfway mark, Australia Under-19 will be a much happier side as they have got 266 runs on the board. England Under-19 bowled well for most of the game but had expensive overs in between and a couple of solid stands have put Australia Under-19 in command here. Australia Under-19 didn't get the best start as they lost Sam Konstas in the very first over for a duck but after this, the skipper Hugh Weibgen and Harry Dixon built up a steady stand worth 105 runs with both batters getting past their individual fifties and kept the scoring rate hovering around 5 runs per over. They lost a few wickets in the middle phase but the skipper anchored the innings really well and notched up a lovely ton after which Ollie Peake and Rafael Macmillan ended the innings with a flourish.

Samuel Badree says that it is an interesting decision to bowl first as this is a bit of a low-scoring surface and more cracks will open up later in the day. The match-up seems to be between the Aussie pacers and the English spinners.

Hugh Weibgen, the Australian skipper says that they were going to have a bat so that worked out alright. Adds that everyone has played their role well and has worked together. Mentions that they were looking to bat first because it has been good in the afternoon and ends by informing that they have made a couple of changes to the team.

He talks about the loss against the West Indies and says they did not bat well in that game but overall had done well so they haven't spoken much on that loss. He then says that this wicket would suit their spinners and that they will have to adapt well to the conditions. He concludes with the one change in the side and says Dominic Kelly will be replaced by Sebastian Morgan.
